correctness.rationale: The geometrically minimal walk covering a finite Munn tree from roots s to t has length 2E-d_T(s,t). The earlier i-conjugacy root-shift criterion restricts root pairs by g0^-1 gi=gn^-1 gj. For fixed free rank, equality of constant-length products of virtual prefix strings is in deterministic logspace by the free-group word problem. Pairwise endpoint comparisons identify first occurrences of undirected edges, and parity of crossings of each distinct edge in the intervening prefix segment computes d_T without storing a path. Nested polynomial loops retain O(log(n+2)) bits. The empty word and r=1 are covered; the result is not a uniform-rank bound. Our distinct checker independently enumerated rank-2 prefix trees through length five and verified the extremal formula; this finite check is not the resource-bound proof.

The edge-parity representation permits reuse in other tree-walk optimization questions; it is not mere renaming of the criterion.
